sounds.intro: Vietnamese uses the Latin alphabet with many accent marks. It has six tones in the north (the south merges some). The mark shows the tone: ma (mid), má (rising), mà (low falling), mả (dipping), mã (broken rising), mạ (low heavy). The same letters with a different tone are different words. Words are short and never change form.
rows: "y" in the north, "z" in the north-west, "y" in the south
like "ch", at the end of a word like "k"
like "ng" in "singer", also at the start of a word
notes: Tones matter more than anything else. "Ma" (ghost), "má" (mother or cheek), "mà" (but), "mả" (tomb), "mã" (horse), "mạ" (rice seedling).
Politeness is built into the pronouns. Choose by age: anh (older man), chị (older woman), em (younger person), ông (old man), bà (old woman), bạn (friend of the same age).

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Vietnamese pronouns depend on age and relationship. "Tôi" is a neutral I. "Bạn" is you for a friend of the same age. For older people use kinship words: anh (older brother, any young man), chị (older sister), ông (grandfather, old man), bà (grandmother, old woman). Younger people are "em".
ex: cô ấy là chị gái của tôi
koh ay lah chee gie koo-ah TOY

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Nouns never change. Use "những" or "các" before the noun for a plural: những cuốn sách (the books). After a number, a classifier word goes between the number and the noun.
ex: một ngôi nhà, những ngôi nhà
moht ngoy nyah, nyoong ngoy NYAH
một cuốn sách, những cuốn sách
moht kwon sahk, nyoong kwon SAHK
một con mèo, những con mèo
moht kon mew, nyoong kon MEW

grammar.title: To be: là, ở, thì
text: "Là" links two nouns (I am a student). Adjectives need no verb. For places use "ở" (at).

grammar.title: Having: có
text: "Có" means to have and also "there is". Put it before the thing.
ex: tôi có một chiếc xe hơi
toy kaw moht chiek seh HUHY

grammar.title: Present tense
text: Verbs never change. "Tôi ăn", "anh ăn" and "họ ăn" all use "ăn". Add "đang" before the verb to say it is happening now.
ex: cô ấy làm việc ở ngân hàng
koh ay lahm viek uh nguhn HAHNG

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The order is subject, verb, object, just as in English. Adjectives come after the noun.

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put "không" before the verb or adjective. For the past, use "chưa" (not yet) or "không" with "đã".
ex: I do not have a car
anh ấy làm việc vào chủ nhật
ahn ay lahm viek vow choo NHUHT
he does not work on Sundays
anh ấy không làm việc vào chủ nhật
ahn ay khohm lahm viek vow choo NHUHT

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add "không" at the end of the sentence for a yes or no question. Reply with the verb: "Bạn đi không?" "Đi." (yes) or "Không đi." (no).
ex: đây có phải sách của bạn không?
day kaw fie sahk koo-ah bahn KHOHM
bạn có nói tiếng Anh không?
bahn kaw noy tiung ahn KHOHM

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stay in the place of the answer. "Bạn tên là gì?" is literally "you name be what?".

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Put "của" (of) between the owned thing and the owner: sách của tôi (book of me). In speech "của" is often dropped.

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: Politeness is shown by pronouns and by "ạ" at the end of a sentence for elders. Say "dạ" for yes to an older person, "vâng" in the north.
ex: ong / bah kaw KHWEH khohm AH

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: No verb changes. Past: put "đã" before the verb. Future: put "sẽ" before the verb.
ex: chúng tôi đã đi công viên
choong toy dah dee kong VIEN
cô ấy đã viết một lá thư
koh ay dah viet moht lah TOO

grammar.title: Commands
text: Use the bare verb. Add "đi" at the end to make it friendlier, or "xin" at the start to be polite. To forbid, put "đừng" in front.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: "Có thể" (can), "phải" (must) and "muốn" (want) go before the main verb. "Không thể" means cannot.
ex: I do not want to eat
hôm nay tôi phải làm việc
hohm nie toy fie lahm VIEK

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Vietnamese uses little words before the place: "ở" (at), "trong" (in), "trên" (on), "dưới" (under), "cạnh" (next to), "gần" (near).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
cửa hàng ở cạnh ngân hàng
koo-ah hahng uh kahng nguhn HAHNG
the park is near the station
công viên ở gần nhà ga
kong vien uh guhn nyah GAH
chúng ta gặp nhau vào buổi sáng
choong tah gahp nyow vow bwoy SAHNG
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Put "hơn" (more) after the adjective: to hơn (bigger). For "the most", put "nhất" after it: to nhất. "Than" is "hơn" and the second item follows.
ex: cái này tốt hơn cái kia
kie nie toht huhn kie KEE-ah
cái này tệ hơn cái kia
kie nie teh huhn kie KEE-ah
